Rules:
- Use ONLY the picked ingredients (by "id") and the cupboard staples (by "id"). Never introduce any other food: no unpicked fruit, vegetable, stock, garlic, herb, spice, sauce or anything else, anywhere in any text. Water, salt and black-pepper are always free. At most 4 of butter, plain-flour, cooking-oil, granulated-sugar and milk may be used in one concept, and only when they are not already picked.
- Ordinary cooking language is always fine ("crisp", "golden", "juices", "gravy" or "broth" made from the dish's own picks, "oil" or "onion" when a picked item is that). Write a picked item by its full name or its last word ("peanut flour" or "flour", never "peanut"; "date syrup", never "date"): the first word of a picked name on its own names a different food. The check only looks for a real FOOD that is neither picked nor a staple, so never name one. Sides and components count: no flatbread, pastry, scone, croutons, crisps, salsa, relish, cream, custard, syrup, caramel, dumplings, noodles, cabbage, bechamel, pickle, wafer, crackers, curd or sugar unless that exact item is picked or a staple. Describe each dish using only the picked items. Before you answer, re-read every title, vibe, description and challengeNote and delete any food word that is not the name of a picked item or a chosen staple (a sauce, side, filling, topping, dough, garnish or flavour you did not pick still counts).
- Each concept uses at least 7 of the ten picked ingredients, at least one uses 8 or more, and between them the three concepts use all ten.
- The three concepts must be genuinely different: three different (dishType, technique) pairs and at least two different dishType values.
- "omitted" lists every picked ingredient the concept does NOT use (exactly the complement of "pickedIngredientIds"), each with a short reason. NEVER mention an omitted ingredient anywhere except inside its own omitted "reason".
- Put ONLY picked ingredient ids in "pickedIngredientIds" and ONLY unpicked cupboard staple ids in "stapleIds" (never a staple id in pickedIngredientIds). Before you answer, count each concept's pickedIngredientIds: every one needs 7 or more and at least one needs 8 or more.
- Write "title", "vibe" and "description" naming only foods the concept uses. British English, plain text, no markdown.

Your FINAL message must be exactly one JSON object and nothing else (no text before or after it, no markdown fences):

{"concepts": [ {"id": "a" | "b" | "c",
   "title": string (1-90 chars),
   "vibe": string (1-40 chars),
   "dishType": one of bowl, traybake, stew, soup, salad, pie, pasta, rice, flatbread, sandwich, pancake, fritter, omelette, bake, dessert, platter,
   "technique": one of roast, bake, pan-fry, simmer, steam, grill, no-cook, mixed,
   "description": string (20-500 chars),
   "pickedIngredientIds": [picked ingredient ids used],
   "stapleIds": [staple ids used, excluding any id already in pickedIngredientIds],
   "omitted": [ {"id": picked id not used, "reason": string (1-140 chars)} ]} ]}  (exactly three concepts, ids a, b and c)

BASKET_JSON: {"ingredients":[{"id":"acorn-squash","name":"Acorn squash","category":"vegetables","blurb":"Ridged squash, roast halved with butter"},{"id":"andouille-sausage","name":"Andouille sausage","category":"meat-poultry","blurb":"Smoky, coarse sausage with Cajun heat"},{"id":"flat-leaf-parsley","name":"Flat-leaf parsley","category":"herbs-aromatics","blurb":"Clean, grassy leaves; chop into sauces, salads and finish almost any savoury dish"},{"id":"gruyere","name":"Gruyère","category":"dairy-eggs","blurb":"Nutty, savoury Swiss cheese for fondue and French onion soup"},{"id":"red-onion","name":"Red onion","category":"vegetables","blurb":"Mild and sharp, lovely raw or pickled"},{"id":"smoked-paprika","name":"Smoked paprika","category":"spices-seasonings","blurb":"Oak-smoked, brick-red powder with a barbecue depth"},{"id":"sourdough-loaf","name":"Sourdough loaf","category":"grains-bakery","blurb":"Tangy, chewy and blistered, brilliant under avocado or cheese"},{"id":"tenderstem-broccoli","name":"Tenderstem broccoli","category":"vegetables","blurb":"Slender sweet stems, quick to cook"},{"id":"tinned-baked-beans","name":"Tinned baked beans","category":"prepared-pantry","blurb":"Haricot beans in sweet tomato sauce; the heart of beans on toast"},{"id":"white-miso","name":"White miso","category":"sauces-stocks-fermented","blurb":"Sweet, mild miso for soups and dressings"}],"staples":[{"id":"water","name":"Water"},{"id":"salt","name":"Salt"},{"id":"black-pepper","name":"Black pepper"},{"id":"butter","name":"Butter"},{"id":"plain-flour","name":"Plain flour"},{"id":"cooking-oil","name":"Cooking oil"},{"id":"granulated-sugar","name":"Granulated sugar"}],"twists":{"forbidden":["milk"]}}

Rules:
- Use ONLY the picked ingredients (by "id") and the cupboard staples (by "id"). Never introduce any other food: no unpicked fruit, vegetable, stock, garlic, herb, spice, sauce or anything else, anywhere in any text. Water, salt and black-pepper are always free. At most 4 of butter, plain-flour, cooking-oil and granulated-sugar may be used in one concept, and only when they are not already picked.
- Ordinary cooking language is always fine ("crisp", "golden", "juices", "gravy" or "broth" made from the dish's own picks, "oil" or "onion" when a picked item is that). Write a picked item by its full name or its last word ("peanut flour" or "flour", never "peanut"; "date syrup", never "date"): the first word of a picked name on its own names a different food. The check only looks for a real FOOD that is neither picked nor a staple, so never name one. Sides and components count: no flatbread, pastry, scone, croutons, crisps, salsa, relish, cream, custard, syrup, caramel, dumplings, noodles, cabbage, bechamel, pickle, wafer, crackers, curd or sugar unless that exact item is picked or a staple. Describe each dish using only the picked items. Before you answer, re-read every title, vibe, description and challengeNote and delete any food word that is not the name of a picked item or a chosen staple (a sauce, side, filling, topping, dough, garnish or flavour you did not pick still counts).
- Each concept uses at least 7 of the ten picked ingredients, at least one uses 8 or more, and between them the three concepts use all ten.
- The three concepts must be genuinely different: three different (dishType, technique) pairs and at least two different dishType values.
- "omitted" lists every picked ingredient the concept does NOT use (exactly the complement of "pickedIngredientIds"), each with a short reason. NEVER mention an omitted ingredient anywhere except inside its own omitted "reason".
- Put ONLY picked ingredient ids in "pickedIngredientIds" and ONLY unpicked cupboard staple ids in "stapleIds" (never a staple id in pickedIngredientIds). Before you answer, count each concept's pickedIngredientIds: every one needs 7 or more and at least one needs 8 or more.
- Write "title", "vibe" and "description" naming only foods the concept uses. British English, plain text, no markdown.

NEVER use or mention these removed ingredients anywhere, not even as a cupboard staple: Milk.

Your FINAL message must be exactly one JSON object and nothing else (no text before or after it, no markdown fences):

{"concepts": [ {"id": "a" | "b" | "c",
   "title": string (1-90 chars),
   "vibe": string (1-40 chars),
   "dishType": one of bowl, traybake, stew, soup, salad, pie, pasta, rice, flatbread, sandwich, pancake, fritter, omelette, bake, dessert, platter,
   "technique": one of roast, bake, pan-fry, simmer, steam, grill, no-cook, mixed,
   "description": string (20-500 chars),
   "pickedIngredientIds": [picked ingredient ids used],
   "stapleIds": [staple ids used, excluding any id already in pickedIngredientIds],
   "omitted": [ {"id": picked id not used, "reason": string (1-140 chars)} ]} ]}  (exactly three concepts, ids a, b and c)
